For an overview of these estimates, see Cannon and BYU Studies staff, “Seventy Contemporaneous Priesthood Restoration Documents,” 222–25; see also Larry C. Porter, “Dating the Restoration of the Melchizedek Priesthood,”Ensign,June 1979, 4–10; Richard Lyman Bushman,Joseph Smith: Rough Stone Rolling(New York: Knopf, 2005), 116–18, and 588, note 35. In the 1880s, Addison Everett gave two accounts that he said were based on details he heard Joseph Smith convey in 1844. Some have interpreted the Everett documents to indicate an 1830 date for the vision, but the accounts are secondhand, have inconsistencies, and were given decades after Joseph Smith’s telling and a half century after the appearance of the angels. For the full texts of both of Everett’s accounts, see Brian Q. Cannon and BYU Studies staff, “Seventy Contemporaneous Priesthood Restoration Documents,” in John W. Welch, ed.,Opening the Heavens: Accounts of Divine Manifestations, 1820–1844(Provo, Utah: Brigham Young University Press, 2005), 228–30, note 11.
